argument_review: A.1: intrinsic spray from the connector, maximal intervals by union and uniqueness; full open maximal flow domain by finite uniformly valid local-flow compositions; zero-velocity case.
A.2: maximal scaling intervals including negative scalars, star-shaped full exponential domain, completeness equivalence, and regular reparametrization with the nonconstant hypothesis.

A.3: all connections sharing affinely parametrized geodesics differ by an alternating tensor; unique torsion-free representative; converse smooth spray via differentiation twice at zero and the full coordinate transition.

A.4: real exponential and logarithm justified from earlier ODE/inverse calculus; explicit solution, maximal finite boundary, full time-one domain and inverse; incompleteness distinguished from surjectivity.

B.1: vertical differential and endpoint map inverse; radial identity, centre coefficients equal half torsion, and distinction between a local endpoint inverse and uniqueness of all contained segments.
B.2: nonvanishing speed, arclength inverse, unit-direction and logarithmic-speed estimates; displacement contradiction bounds total length and then maximum speed. Zero C and constant paths included.

B.3: compact coefficient bound, squared-coordinate convexity, uniform whole-interval flow neighbourhood, and four simultaneous radius conditions. The speed lemma forces every contained competitor into the endpoint inverse; open star-shaped fibre domain proved explicitly.
B.4: prescribed real/complex frame, linear gauge matrix, invertibility near the point and exact cancellation. Tangent-frame bracket accounts for possible nonzero torsion.
C.1: coordinate signs, curvature derivation on tensor products and duals, cancellation on scalars, and the covariant Hessian torsion correction fully checked.
C.2: expanded cyclic conversion from exterior to tensor covariant derivative; both torsion corrections and all tensor slots accounted for without a torsion-free frame assumption.
C.3: parallel-metric skewness follows from tensor curvature; four explicit cyclic identities give pair interchange only under zero torsion.

D.1: principal and linear transport identified by the initial frame; curvature evaluated on standard horizontal fields gives precisely transported tangent-space curvature, including nonclosed holonomy.

D.2: differentiation in parallel frames identifies all covariant curvature slots with standard-horizontal words; change of horizontal frame gives the same jet span. Exact prior proofs give Lie closure, local stabilization, constant-rank and analytic equality, with connected-component hypotheses and discrete full holonomy distinguished.

D.3: full possibly immersed holonomy reduction carries the restricted connection; parallel tensors have constant frame components; actual vertical/horizontal brackets prove the finite frame algebra and Jacobi, without an unproved global group action.
E.1: Cartesian derivatives give all polar coefficients and the exact cancellation of derivative and commutator curvature terms.
E.2: every cyclic torsion derivative, quadratic correction, endomorphism derivative and curvature-torsion correction independently computed; both corrections are nonzero.

E.3: one-sided smooth flat function gives torsion zero and all curvature jets zero by a derivative-ideal induction. Nilpotent transport solves the full ODE, and arbitrarily small rectangles generate the actual local/restricted/full shear group.

F.1: straight maximal geodesics and full exponential map from the skew bilinear coefficients; torsion, curvature and both full tensor derivatives explicitly calculated. Constant jet rank and contractible loops give the full shear holonomy, with the frame algebra explicitly evaluated.

F.2: complete earlier quotient and flat-connection proof instantiated to the standard torus; full geodesics and exponential map, noninjectivity, and convex-normal uniqueness for every projected ball of radius below one-half proved using its injective lift chart.

F.3: sphere projection connection supplied by exact earlier proofs; constant-speed great-circle solutions and full exponential domain, smooth inverse on the radius-pi ball, curvature sign and metric tensor formula including poles, parallel curvature and oriented area, and all holonomy groups SO(2), with connectedness explicitly proved.

G.1: standard-horizontal projection is geodesic; exact whole-path lift theorem on compact subintervals and uniqueness glue a lift on the full maximal interval. Velocity identification and maximality prove equality of intervals, including zero.

G.2: tensor coordinate formula derived factor by factor; every exterior argument-derivative term paired with its opposite-order partner with the explicit signs i+j-1 and i+j. Bracket subtraction leaves torsion with sign i+j+1; degree zero and scalar cases included.

G.3: all four rotation-matrix derivatives and the frame bracket checked. The variable 3D potential gives zero torsion at the origin but cyclic curvature e1; full tensor derivative and both Bianchi hypotheses distinguished.

G.4: finite spanning list and maximal order at a point; independent smooth generators and a pivot/minor argument prove lower semicontinuity. The parallel-frame argument applies separately to each tensor on the full reachable reduction.
G.5: quotient return criterion gives full periodicity. Both specified velocities evaluated; positive square-root existence and elementary minimal-denominator irrationality proof supplied.
G.6: coordinate vectors obtained from the already proved orthonormal sphere frame, then all four derivative pairs calculated with the product rule and chart restriction.
